response.sql:
WITH trans_sentiment AS (
  SELECT 
    tr.transreg,
    tr.ordertypedist,
    AVG(sf.shortintrt) AS trans_avg_shortint,
    AVG(sf.optvolrt) AS trans_avg_optvolrt
  FROM transactionrecord tr
  INNER JOIN sentimentandfundamentals sf ON tr.transreg = sf.transref
  GROUP BY tr.transreg, tr.ordertypedist
),
ordertype_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    tr.ordertypedist,
    AVG(sf.shortintrt) AS ordertype_avg_shortint
  FROM transactionrecord tr
  INNER JOIN sentimentandfundamentals sf ON tr.transreg = sf.transref
  GROUP BY tr.ordertypedist
)
SELECT 
  ts.transreg,
  ts.ordertypedist,
  ts.trans_avg_shortint,
  ts.trans_avg_optvolrt,
  CASE 
    WHEN oa.ordertype_avg_shortint IS NULL OR oa.ordertype_avg_shortint = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ts.trans_avg_shortint / oa.ordertype_avg_shortint
  END AS shortint_ratio
FROM trans_sentiment ts
LEFT JOIN ordertype_avg oa ON ts.ordertypedist = oa.ordertypedist
ORDER BY 
  shortint_ratio IS NULL,
  shortint_ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A transaction may have multiple sentiment records; I compute one average per transaction (aggregating shortintrt and optvolrt across all sentiment records for that transaction), then compare to the order type average.
The "average short interest for its order type mix" is computed across all sentiment records for all transactions sharing that order type (not averaging per-transaction values separately).
The ratio expresses the transaction's average short interest relative to its order type: transaction_avg / ordertype_avg.

alternatives.interpretation: Compute one ratio per sentiment record, rather than aggregating to one row per transaction. This would result in one output row per sentiment record, with the ratio comparing that record's shortintrt value (not an aggregated average) to the order type average.
